category_info.harvest_window: Harvest when silks have turned brown and dry, and kernels release a milky liquid when pierced with a fingernail.
category_info.watering_need: 2.5-4 cm of water per week, critical during silking and ear development

observations.symptom: Rectangular, tan to grayish-brown necrotic lesions bounded by leaf veins
observations.location: Leaf blade surface on both sides of the central midrib
observations.evidence: Distinct blocky, elongated lesions aligned with parallel veins covering a significant portion of the leaf tissue
Foliage shows yellow halos surrounding coalesced dry, dead necrotic patches

possible_causes.name: Gray Leaf Spot (Cercospora zeae-maydis)
possible_causes.reason: The distinctly rectangular, vein-limited, tan-to-gray lesions running parallel to the leaf veins are the definitive hallmark symptom of Cercospora leaf infection in maize.

possible_causes.name: Southern Corn Leaf Blight (Bipolaris maydis)
possible_causes.reason: Can cause elongated, parallel-sided lesions between veins, though typically less rigidly rectangular than gray leaf spot.

possible_causes.name: Bacterial Stripe or Leaf Streak
possible_causes.reason: Bacterial pathogens can produce linear lesions along leaf veins, but typically exhibit water-soaking rather than paper-like dry tan rectangular blocks.

recommended_actions.action: Avoid overhead watering and keep foliage dry
recommended_actions.reason: Fungal spores of Cercospora rely on prolonged leaf wetness and high humidity to infect and spread.

recommended_actions.action: Clean up and dispose of infected crop residue after the season
recommended_actions.reason: The fungus overwinters on infected maize residue left on or near the soil surface.

recommended_actions.action: Implement crop rotation for subsequent plantings
recommended_actions.reason: Rotating away from corn for at least 1-2 years breaks the pathogen life cycle in the soil and garden bed.

seasonal_context: Gray leaf spot typically develops and worsens during warm, humid mid-to-late summer periods, especially in dense plantings.
what_to_monitor: Spread of rectangular lesions to upper canopy leaves near and above the ear
Premature leaf desiccation and lodging of stalks due to lost photosynthetic area
limitations: Microscopic confirmation or fungal spore isolation is needed to definitively differentiate Cercospora species from other fungal foliar blights.
Only a single excised leaf section is shown, preventing assessment of whole-canopy distribution.
follow_up_questions: Is this issue isolated to the lowest leaves or has it spread to leaves above the ear?
Has corn been planted in this exact spot in previous consecutive seasons?
